function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Park Ji‑Sung (박지성)** – *South Korean former professional footballer*  

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | 박지성 (Park Ji‑Sung) |
| **Date of Birth** | March 25, 1981 |
| **Place of Birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Midfielder / Defensive midfielder (often deployed as a “box‑to‑box” playmaker) |

---

### Early Life & Youth Career  
- Grew up in Seoul’s Gangnam district.  
- Joined the youth academy of **Ulsan Hyundai Horang-i** (now Ulsan Hyundai FC) while still in high school.  
- Made senior debut for Ulsan in 1999 at age 18.

### Club Career Highlights  

| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals | Notable Achievements |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|---------------------|
| 2000–2005 | **Ulsan Hyundai** (K League 1) | ~140 | 12 | Won K League titles (2002, 2005); earned domestic reputation as one of Asia’s top midfielders. |
| 2005–2010 | **PSV Eindhoven** (Eredivisie, Netherlands) | 151 | 13 | Key role in winning Eredivisie title (2007–08) and KNVB Cup (2008–09). Became first Asian player to win Dutch league trophy. |
| 2010–2013 | **Tottenham Hotspur** (Premier League, England) | 107 | 11 | First Korean to score in Premier League; helped Spurs reach UEFA Champions League semi‑finals (2012–13). Earned praise for work rate, passing range, and defensive contributions. |
| 2013–2014 | **FC Tokyo** (J.League, Japan) | 30 | 2 | Short stint in Japanese top flight. |
| 2014–2015 | **Ulsan Hyundai** (return) | 28 | 1 | Final playing season before retiring. |

> **Total Professional Caps:** ≈ 470  
> **Total Professional Goals:** ≈ 40+

### International Career  

- Represented South Korea across all levels: U20, U23, Olympic squad, and senior national team.  
- **Senior caps:** 108 appearances, 15 goals.  
- Participated in three FIFA World Cups (2002, 2006, 2010) and two AFC Asian Cups (2004, 2010).  
- Known for leadership on the pitch—captained the national side during several tournaments.  
- Awarded the **FIFA Fair Play award** for sportsmanship in 2006.

### Playing Style & Reputation  

- Renowned for exceptional stamina, tactical intelligence, and versatility.  
- Excelled both defensively (tackles, interceptions) and offensively (through passes, long-range shots).  
- Often described as the “engine room” of teams he played for—a modern box‑to‑box midfielder capable of dictating tempo.  
- One of the most respected Asian players abroad, breaking stereotypes about Asian footballers’ physicality and technical skill.

### Post-Retirement Activities  

- Retired from professional football in December 2015 after a brief comeback attempt.  
- Transitioned into media and punditry: frequent analyst on Korean sports broadcasts covering international leagues.  
- Served briefly as assistant coach for the South Korean national team under head coaches Huh Jung-moo and later Kim Do-hoon.  
- Engaged in philanthropic efforts through the **“Park Ji‑Sung Foundation,”** focusing on youth development programs in South Korea.  
- Holds ambassadorial roles for various brands and has appeared in commercials promoting healthy lifestyles.

### Personal Life  

- Married to actress **Kim Seong‑hee** (not publicly confirmed; some sources suggest she was a close friend rather than spouse).  
- Has two children (a son born in 2010 and a daughter born in 2013).  
- Fluent in English, having spent significant years living in Europe and Japan.  
- Advocates for mental health awareness among athletes, citing his own experiences dealing with pressure and injury setbacks.

---

#### Fun Facts  

1. **First Asian Player to Win Major European Titles** – With PSV’s 2008 Eredivisie triumph.  
2. **Record-Breaking Work Rate** – In the 2011–12 Premier League season, logged over 100 tackles per game, ranking him among the league’s best defenders despite being a midfielder.  
3. **Cultural Impact** – Inspired a generation of young Koreans to pursue careers overseas; numerous academies now feature training modules modeled after his style.  
4. **Nickname** – “The King of the Pitch” (“축구의 왕”) coined by fans due to his dominance in matches.  

--- 

If you’re looking for information on another individual named Ji‑Sung Park (e.g., academics, artists, business figures), let me know which domain you're interested in!
